summary: Real-code evidence for the Display Registry & Monitor Placement phase: assigns a role (Unassigned/Operator/Projector/Stage/Confidence/Lobby) to each physical monitor and places the existing presentation window on the monitor assigned to that screen's role.
trigger: After Phase 3.10.1's pure architecture audit, the user gave a fully detailed specification for Phase 3.10.2, including an explicit instruction not to touch the proven Windows-safe window-creation pipeline (async command -> WebviewWindowBuilder -> position -> build -> resize workaround) and a 6-item scope boundary.

designDecisions.twoDistinctRoleConcepts: DisplayScreen (Phase 3.10: which content stream/window - Stage/Confidence/Lobby) and DisplayRole (this phase: which role a physical monitor plays - Unassigned/Operator/Projector/Stage/Confidence/Lobby) are kept as two separate enums in two modules, connected only by an explicit bridge function display_registry::screen_role (DisplayScreen::Stage maps to DisplayRole::Projector). Chosen over renaming/merging them to avoid silently conflating window identity with monitor role.
designDecisions.honestMonitorIdentity: Tauri exposes no real OS-level stable monitor id. compute_monitor_id prefers the OS-reported name, falls back to a position/resolution fingerprint (unnamed@x,y-WxH). Documented as CIP's own best-effort session identity, not a hardware serial number claim.
designDecisions.oneDeliberateUpsertTable: display_role_assignments uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, the one deviation from this project's append-only-log convention for every other table, because role assignment has current-value (not one-row-per-event) semantics. Documented explicitly in the migration file.
designDecisions.globalNotServiceScoped: Role assignment is a machine property, matching the Phase 3.6 saved_scriptures precedent - not tied to any one church service.
designDecisions.provenPipelineUntouched: open_display_window's async-command/build ordering and its #[cfg(target_os = "windows")] resize-nudge workaround are structurally unchanged - the function only gained an Option<MonitorPlacement> parameter. None (no assigned role, or the assigned monitor is disconnected) reproduces the exact pre-3.10.2 unpositioned 1280x720 window, satisfying the user's explicit 'single-display machines keep working exactly as before' requirement.
designDecisions.dpiCorrectPlacement: Monitor's position/size are physical pixels; WebviewWindowBuilder::position/inner_size expect logical pixels. Placement is converted via Tauri's own PhysicalPosition/PhysicalSize::to_logical (not a hand-rolled division) to avoid an off-by-scale-factor bug on a non-100%-scaled monitor. The pre-existing Windows resize-nudge workaround, previously hardcoded to 1280x720, now consumes the same logical_size actually used to build the window - fixing a latent defect that would have silently fought new placement sizing on Windows specifically.
designDecisions.noLiteralFullscreen: This phase positions/sizes the window to the monitor's full bounds but does not call a platform fullscreen API - judged a separate, riskier decision, documented as a known limitation rather than silently decided.
